plain_description.what: Comparing split rules for building the tree, always splitting each node in two. Gaussian-mixture splits (diagonal or full covariance) are compared with a spherical k-means split that mimics the engine. Done on MASSIVE, CLINC and MMLU-Pro with the same number of leaves and 5 seeds.
plain_description.why: It asks whether a more flexible split rule would give better partitions than what the engine uses.
plain_description.information: A clear win would make a mixture-based split a candidate for a new, separately approved test (never a direct engine change). Result (no new calls): no mixture rule clearly beat the k-means stand-in. The full-covariance rule led on CLINC but fell just short of the seed-to-seed spread. On MASSIVE the bar was out of reach. Its leads are descriptive only, and 'no win' is not proof of a tie.
